- Overestimate prices in the short term after sentiment spikes (especially >0.3) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate downward moves when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.18) — model fails to anticipate sharp drops.
- Lag in price corrections: model often lags 1–3 days behind true price reversals, especially after sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to revert to historical mean when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Overshoot after spikes: if sentiment rises sharply, model forecasts a peak that is too high and then underestimates the subsequent decline.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in the first 5–7 days after sentiment spikes, then converge — model overreacts to sentiment-driven momentum.
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment > 0.3, model tends to overforecast price increases; when sentiment < 0.1, underforecast drops — model is sensitive to sentiment but not calibrated to magnitude.
